Left, prominent_group(2) finds the pair E, B (accent), which together lie on 0.65 of the shortest paths between the other five nodes. Right, E and F, two of the three nodes with the highest individual betweenness, cover much of the same traffic, so as a group they score only 0.40." width="100%"} `group_betweenness_centrality()` scores a group you choose; this method finds the best group of a given size: the `k` nodes that, together, lie on the largest share of shortest paths between the other nodes. The best group is usually not the `k` individually most central nodes, because two hubs on the same routes intercept the same traffic. Typical uses are placing `k` monitors, checkpoints or brokers so that between them they see as much of the network's traffic as possible. "Shortest" follows `shortest_path()`: hops on an unweighted graph, total weight on a weighted one. Scaling is the same as in `group_betweenness_centrality()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [k]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The group size (at least 1). [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to measure path length by edge weight. If `None` (default), follows the graph. [exclude]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Nodes that may not be chosen, as integer IDs or string labels. Paths through them still count. Default is `None` (any node may be chosen). [endpoints]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, also count pairs with an endpoint in the group. Default is `False`. [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), divide by `(n - k)(n - k - 1)` so the score lies in `[0, 1]`. NetworkX 3.7 uses the same divisor with `endpoints=True`, so EdgeCase does too, although the score can then exceed 1. `group_betweenness_centrality(endpoints=True)` divides by `n(n - 1)` instead, so set `normalized=False` to compare the two. [greedy]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, add the node with the largest gain one at a time instead of searching exhaustively. Much faster on large graphs, but the group may not be the best one. Default is `False`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tuple[float, list[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The group betweenness of the best group and its node IDs, in the order the search chose them. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `k` is less than 1 or more than the number of nodes that may be chosen, a node in `exclude=` does not exist, or weights are used and one is negative. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The search is the depth-first branch and bound of Puzis, Elovici and Dolev (2007). It precomputes the path betweenness of every pair of candidates (the share of shortest paths through both) in $O(V^3)$; adding a member updates that matrix in $O(V^2)$ to count only paths avoiding the group, and a branch is pruned when its value plus the `k` best remaining gains cannot beat the best group so far. The search is exact; its result always equals `group_betweenness_centrality()` of the group returned. ## Examples {.doc-examples} In two triangles joined by a path, the best pair is the two ends of the path, which between them sit on every route from one triangle to the other: ::: {#e757947b .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "G"), ("G", "E")]) ) score, group = graph.prominent_group(2) round(score, 3), [graph.get_label_from_id(n) for n in group] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (0.8, ['E', 'C']) ``` ::: ::: ## Notes {.doc-notes} NetworkX's `prominent_group()` subtracts the paths with an endpoint in the group only after the search, which picks the wrong group on disconnected and directed graphs, where that count depends on the group. It also halves the path counts on weighted graphs and never completes a group from exactly the remaining candidates. EdgeCase's search avoids all three and agrees with an exhaustive search over every group; NetworkX also rounds the score to two decimals.
